items.question: My K1 class has outdoor play in 20 minutes. 24-hr PSI is 49 in the north. Do I cancel?
items.rationale: The 24-hour PSI reading of 49 falls within the Good band (0–50). At this band level, the health advisory for vulnerable persons—which governs preschool cohorts entirely composed of children—permits normal outdoor activities. No minimisation or substitution is required. Outdoor play in 20 minutes may proceed as scheduled.

items.question: My K1 class has outdoor play in 20 minutes. 24-hr PSI is 51 in the north. Do I cancel?
items.rationale: The 24-hour PSI reading of 51 places the activity in the Moderate band (51–100). At this band, ECDA guidance states that outdoor play and excursions proceed normally for preschool cohorts. Although preschool children are a vulnerable group under the NEA health advisory, the Moderate band does not trigger restrictions on outdoor activity. The standing requirement for daily physical activity continues. You do not need to cancel the outdoor play session in 20 minutes. Ensure the air-conditioned room with an air purifier remains available for any child who becomes unwell during or after the session.
items.notes: Boundary item: PSI 51 is moderate. Adjacent value flips the band.

items.question: 24-hr PSI is 51. Does the Sec 2 PE lesson outdoors go ahead?
items.rationale: The 24-hour PSI of 51 falls within the Moderate band (51–100). At this band, the health advisory for healthy persons and the school guidance both permit normal outdoor activities. The Sec 2 PE lesson outdoors proceeds as scheduled. Teachers should continue to monitor any students who are unwell or have pre-existing lung or heart conditions.

items.question: 24-hr PSI reads 51. Can my crew continue the outdoor rebar work?
items.rationale: At 24-hour PSI 51 (Moderate band, 51–100), the published guidance permits outdoor work to proceed normally for both healthy and susceptible employees. No haze-specific restriction on outdoor work applies at this band. The employer's obligation is to have preparatory measures in place — susceptible employee identification, pre-set restriction criteria, fit-tested masks, and adequate stock — so that the operation can respond appropriately if the PSI rises into the Unhealthy band or above. The general duty under the WSH Act to assess and manage risks remains in force; "no haze-specific restriction" does not mean "no duty". For rebar work, which is typically prolonged and strenuous, the crew may continue, but the employer should ensure that if conditions deteriorate, the measures to reduce duration and intensity (for healthy employees) or minimise exposure (for susceptible employees) can be deployed without delay.
